title: Boot-hedge staggered snapshot loader for reduced cold-start tail and bounded throughput guarantees
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: Customers using Dedicated capacity report intermittent cold-start spikes that breach per-tenant tail latency SLOs during bursty onboarding. Existing warm-pools populate weights eagerly but indiscriminately, causing oversubscription of memory/GPU bandwidth and unpredictable eviction cascades for KV caches. Goal: implement a lightweight, boot-hedge snapshot loader that performs staggered, tenant-aware weight and KV-snapshot activation tied to committed throughput guarantees and autoscaler signals. The loader must reduce 99.9th tail latency for cold attach events by >60% without increasing overall memory pressure beyond existing warm-pool budgets. Approach: 1) Create compact snapshot artifacts (delta snapshots + compressed KV fingerprints) that can be staged on node-local SSD and streamed with prioritized shards. 2) Implement a staggered admission controller that spreads activation across a configurable window (default 45s) weighted by tenant SLA/commitment and real-time throughput backing. 3) Integrate with autoscaler signal bus so snapshot activation urgency increases when scaling is required and decreases when autoscaler is in conservative mode. 4) Adopt a two-phase KV priming sequence: fast fingerprint hydration (low bandwidth) followed by progressive KV page materialization (bandwidth-heavy) only when request traffic crosses per-tenant thresholds. 5) Add soft admission tickets to prevent hot-shard storms and enable graceful degradation: if snapshot activation would exceed node I/O budget, fallback to lightweight micro-quantized model variant. Trade-offs considered: aggressive prewarming improves latency but increases network/storage IOPS and can conflict with other tenants on shared nodes. We will bias by customer commitment and enable config knobs per-dedicated-fleet. Deliverables: - snapshot manifest format and compact on-disk representation - admission controller service with tenant-priority policy - KV fingerprint preloader and progressive page hydrator - metrics and dashboards for cold-start tail, I/O budget, and priming success rate - migration plan for existing warm-pools to opt-in staged activation
acceptance_criteria: 99.9th tail cold-start latency for tenant attach reduces by >=60% in synthetic replay (95% CI)
Priming I/O does not increase average node SSD bandwidth >15% during steady state
No regression in steady-state throughput for other tenants on shared nodes (<=2% variance)
Feature is controllable via fleet policy flags and per-tenant runtime knobs in Console
Automated e2e test that replays burst attach and validates graceful fallback to micro-quantized variant
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement snapshot loader behind feature flag and run on 2 dedicated fleets with synthetic replay traffic (metrics-only). Phase 2 (controlled opt-in): allow customers with committed throughput to opt-in via Console and default to enabled for fleets with SLA >= dedicated-annual. Phase 3 (broader): automatic tiered activation based on historical attach pattern signals and autoscaler harmonization. At each phase we monitor cold_start.p99.9_ms and priming.fallback_count and require green for 48h before expanding. Provide kill-switch at fleet controller and revert to previous warm-pool priming within 5 minutes.
